## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-juan late-Míng compendium of brief biographies of eminent Míng-dynasty monks, compiled by Yúnqī Zhūhóng — one of the Four Great Masters of the Late Míng (*wǎn Míng sì dàshī* 晚明四大師, alongside [德清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%B7%E6%B8%85) Hānshān Déqīng, [真可](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E5%8F%AF) Zǐbǎi Zhēnkě, and [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) Ǒuyì Zhìxù). Title — "Brief Compilation of Famous Monks of the Imperial Míng" — frames it as an internal Míng-Buddhist memorial work.

**Abstract**

Zhūhóng selects and briefly summarises the biographies of approximately two dozen eminent Míng monks across multiple traditions (Chán, Pure Land, Vinaya, doctrinal). The compilation reflects Zhūhóng's broadly inclusive late-Míng Buddhist programme, in which Chán practice, Pure Land devotion, and scholastic learning were treated as complementary rather than alternative options. The brevity and selectivity make this a teaching work rather than a comprehensive biographical record.
